ParkFlow makes one parking zone bookable: reserve ahead, get verified at the gate, and park in any free bay.
This is the LG level at KLGCC Mall, filmed on site and rebuilt in 3D. The whole level becomes the Priority Zone.
Our prototype already runs the booking flow, from the home screen to a live view of the zone.
A shopper taps Book, picks an arrival time and confirms. Members have the fee credited to their parking bill; non-members pay it on top. Their number plate is the pass.
Behind it, a controller links KLGCC's existing cameras, barrier, membership and payments. Members pay the fee or the bill, whichever is larger.
Every bay has a state: grey is occupied, amber is protected for bookings, green is open to walk-ins.
A booking is a commitment. Every fifteen minutes, the planner looks three hours ahead and decides how many bays to protect.
At nine it's quiet, so a hundred spaces stay open to walk-ins.
By ten-thirty, bookings are building. The forecast updates, and more bays turn amber.
No-show after fifteen minutes? The bay goes back to walk-ins.
At noon, walk-in entry closes. Walk-ins go to general parking, and every booking is still honoured.
A booked driver arrives at the same entrance. The plate is read, the booking is verified, and the car parks in any free bay.
Operators get one view of capacity, plans and exceptions, with every decision logged.
Your parking data tells you more than you think.
